newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire-Tyne seeks more from Laser.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire-Tyne seeks more from Laser.

text.p: Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television called on Tuesday for an improved performance from the Laser airtime sales house, a subsidiary of Granada Group.
The company said it was disappointed that its share of commercial television (ITV) advertising revenue had dipped to 10.22 percent in the first half of 1996 from 10.67 percent for 1995 as a whole.

"This is a blip rather than a stagnation but it is not the level of growth we would have expected," Yorkshire finance director Nick Castro told a news conference. The company's advertising revenue totalled 84.6 million stg in the first half.
Yorkshire chairman and chief executive Ward Thomas noted that Laser's contract with Yorkshire expired at the end of 1997 and could be terminated at six months' notice.
He said that Laser had set a target for a 10.9 percent share of ITV advertising revenue this year and doubted whether this could now be met.
There is a financial penalty for failure to deliver on the target but Thomas said it was not substantial.
The company covers some 15 percent of the UK population and Thomas said the target was to restore its advertising share to the 14 percent level reached some years ago.
